Subject: Interim-relief clause and forum — redlines attached

Karthik —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Our GC has reviewed the MSA and flagged two urgent items we need to lock before the order form signs: (1) interim injunctive relief carve (we need explicit preservation language and a US federal/CA state court option for immediate preservation) and (2) forum for disputes (we want California state court exclusive for enforcement of injunctive relief).

Attached is Astra's redline (ASTRA_MSA_redline_v2.pdf) with in-line comments. We're conscious of your team’s preference for arbitration for most disputes, so we tried to carve only the interim preservation path — but GC insists on a path to immediate court access for preservation and to enforce subpoenas to third parties.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept a limited carve for injunctive relief and a short notice period (24 hours) for preservation requests? If not, outline what alternate language would get us to sign this week.

Claire
Senior Contracts Manager
Astra Logistics

Claire —

Appreciate the redline and the clear ask. We're absolutely open to a narrowly tailored interim-relief carve that preserves your ability to seek emergency relief in court. A couple of immediate clarifications so we can get legal to sign off quickly: 

- Is Astra asking for exclusive preservation jurisdiction in California (i.e., preserving state court for interim measures) while keeping arbitration for merits?
- When you say "24 hours" notice, do you mean notice to Redwood operations to preserve KV-cache/state or notice to legal with a request to initiate emergency filings? Practically we need a narrow operations-preservation SLA (we can commit to 48 hours for a cache-dump plus expedited access) and a legal carve that allows filing in state court for injunctive relief.

Laura / Marissa — looping you both. Laura, can infra commit to a 48-hour preservation turnaround and a one-time emergency export? Marissa, can you weigh in on whether we can accept an explicit California preservation carve and still preserve arbitration for underlying disputes?

I'll consolidate and propose redline language for Astra by EOD.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interim-relief clause and forum — redlines attached

Karthik —

We can do a one-time emergency export of customer data and KV cache within 48 hours of receipt of a preservation request that includes a court order or attorney declaration. Operational notes: 

- Export will be a best-effort snapshot of model state and logs (we can't guarantee realtime sync for in-flight requests).
- We will require a signed confidentiality addendum for the exported artifacts (we can provide a standard form).
- For subpoenas to third parties, we will cooperate but need a court order or narrowly tailored request; we cannot proactively reach into partner systems without legal process.

Marissa — legal side: my read is we can accept a carved exception that allows immediate court filings for injunctive relief (CA state or federal) provided: 
1) the carve applies only to injunctive relief and evidence preservation; 2) all merits claims remain subject to arbitration; and 3) Redwood retains the right to seek a stay of any non-final remedies sought in court.

I'll attach a short paragraph we can propose to Astra that codifies the above. Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@astralogistics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Interim-relief clause and forum — proposed limited carve

Claire / Astra Legal —

Thanks for the quick review. Per our internal alignment, please find proposed language below which we believe balances Astra's need for immediate preservation with Redwood's arbitration-first dispute framework. If this looks acceptable we can stitch it into the MSA redline and release for signature: 

--- proposed clause (for insertion into Section 18: Dispute Resolution) ---
Notwithstanding Section 18.2 (Arbitration of Disputes), the parties agree that either party may seek emergency injunctive or other provisional relief in the state or federal courts located in the State of California for the limited purpose of preservation of evidence, protection of Redwood’s systems, or preservation of either party’s confidential information. The foregoing shall not be construed as a waiver of the right to arbitrate the merits of any dispute, and the parties agree that any such emergency proceedings shall be limited to provisional relief only; all other claims shall proceed to arbitration in accordance with Section 18.2. Redwood shall, upon receipt of a written preservation request accompanied by a court order or sworn attorney declaration, use commercially reasonable efforts to produce an export of relevant data and logs within forty-eight (48) hours. Any production under this paragraph shall be subject to the parties’ confidentiality protections.
--- end proposed clause ---

If Astra needs the preservation jurisdiction to be expressly "exclusive" to California for injunctive relief, note that creates operational complexity for multi-jurisdictional Astra entities. We prefer language that permits filings in California courts but does not require exclusivity.

Please confirm and we'll update the MSA redline in Drive and send a clean copy for signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
